articles.title: Home Assistant’s installer rechecks a drive before erasing it
articles.dek: A fresh identity check helps prevent an installation from wiping a replacement drive.
body: Home Assistant’s installer checks that the selected drive is still connected and matches its recorded identity before erasing it. Previously, unplugging a selected USB drive and inserting another could give the replacement the same system address, causing the installer to erase the wrong disk.

Bram Kragten adds checks before opening the erase confirmation and again when it is confirmed, comparing the drive’s system address, model, vendor and size. A missing or changed drive sends the user back to selection, while the confirmation identifies the drive being erased.
The installer also stops showing a misleading Cancel control during a new write after an earlier attempt failed. This does not add the ability to cancel a write already in progress.

pullRequests.title: Guard the erase against a stale or mistaken drive selection (#47: F8, F10, F11)

articles.title: Home Assistant puts light colours directly on dashboard tiles
articles.dek: A sliding colour strip preserves fine control even in narrow cards.
body: Home Assistant adds a light-colour control directly to dashboard tiles. Moving the colour strip changes the light’s hue, while an optional second slider changes saturation, avoiding a separate light-control dialog for those adjustments.

Paul Bottein keeps the chosen hue beneath a fixed window: a wide tile shows the full spectrum, and a narrow one shows a closer view with the same precision. A tile can show hue, saturation or both; when both are enabled, tapping the compact control swaps which one is expanded.

pullRequests.title: Add light color card feature with hue scrubber
Add light color card feature

articles.title: Hydro-Québec peak periods become inputs for Home Assistant automations
articles.dek: Public event times help households prepare for winter demand peaks without sharing account credentials.
body: Home Assistant adds Hydro-Québec’s peak-demand event times as inputs for automations. Households can use them to prepare before a winter peak, such as preheating a home before reducing consumption during an event.

The new connection reads the utility’s public data feed without a Hydro-Québec account. Customers enrolled in eligible peak-saving offers can use the times to help plan around those programs; this connection supplies event timestamps rather than enrolling anyone or calculating savings. Beat makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the integration.

pullRequests.title: Add Hydro-Quebec Peak Events integration

articles.title: Matter.js enforces time limits on lock PIN access
articles.dek: Lock implementations using the library reject PIN requests outside their schedules and after temporary access expires.
body: Lock developers using Matter.js gain enforcement of PIN schedules and temporary-access deadlines. Its door-lock implementation previously accepted a valid enabled PIN without checking whether its allowed time window had ended, and temporary users never expired after their first successful use.

Ludovic BOUÉ makes scheduled access depend on the host’s local clock and saves a temporary user’s expiry deadline across restarts. An expired PIN is rejected even before the timer marks the account disabled. Ingo Fischer reviewed the correction.
The correction applies to PIN requests sent to the Matter.js implementation. Physical keypad, fingerprint and other local credential checks remain separate.

pullRequests.title: fix(node): enforce DoorLock schedule restrictions and ExpiringUser timeout

articles.title: Home Assistant starts Music Assistant dashboards on household displays
articles.dek: Automations can show a party screen, music quiz or a chosen player’s now-playing view.
body: Home Assistant gains controls for Music Assistant’s dashboard displays, including compatible Chromecasts and kiosk browsers. Automations can show a party dashboard, a music quiz or a selected player’s now-playing screen, then hide it again.

Marvin Schenkel represents each display as a media player. Its media browser lists the dashboards that display supports and provides a player picker for now-playing views; the entity also reflects the active display session and its artwork.

pullRequests.title: Add dashboard display media players to Music Assistant

media.alt: Music Assistant’s Home Assistant media browser offers Party, Music quiz and Now playing dashboards

articles.title: Music Assistant reconnects the car player after a timeout
articles.dek: A stalled connection no longer leaves Android Auto looking ready while playback stays unresponsive.
body: Music Assistant’s mobile player keeps trying after a connection attempt times out, instead of giving up until the app is restarted. The failure could appear after switching off a car or briefly losing the phone’s network connection: Android Auto looked connected but did not respond.

Michael N also makes a failed audio channel reliably announce that it has closed, allowing the player to reconnect. In his Pixel 10 test running Android 17 with both corrections, the player registered again three seconds after the app reconnected.
The timeout correction is Michael N’s first contribution to Music Assistant’s mobile app. Andrii Mitnovych reviewed both changes.

pullRequests.title: Fix local player not reconnecting after a Sendspin connect timeout
Fix WebRTC data channels left half-closed when cleanup is cancelled

articles.title: Music Assistant gives AI clients broader controls and individual access
articles.dek: Each client gets its own connection token, with policies limiting which commands it may use.
body: Music Assistant’s connection for AI clients replaces a fixed set of twelve tools with discovery across its live command catalogue. Configurable access policies limit which Music Assistant commands a client may use, while a connection wizard issues a separate token for each client.

Mikhail Nevskiy supplies the redesigned connection. Clients that call the former tool names directly must switch to the new search, command-description and command-call tools. Existing library, player and queue resources remain. Marvin Schenkel reviewed the work.

pullRequests.title: Update FastMCP Server provider to v2.1.22

articles.title: Sendspin gives device makers a path for streaming audio in
articles.dek: The C++ library gains audio capture support, with PCM and Opus paths and a desktop example.
body: Device makers using Sendspin’s C++ library gain the ability to send captured audio to a compatible server, extending the library beyond receiving playback. The new source role carries timestamped audio in uncompressed PCM or, when the server supports it, the low-delay Opus format.

Kevin Ahrendt builds on source-role work co-authored with Chris Uthe. A desktop example takes audio from the computer’s default input device, starting and stopping capture when the server requests it. The implementation also handles interrupted capture without replaying an old backlog.

The new path is for applications built on the library. Automated tests and ESP32 builds pass, but the desktop example has not been exercised against a live server, and on-device Opus performance still needs measurement.

articles.title: Home Assistant fixes network loss on affected VLAN setups
articles.dek: A Supervisor setting could leave some Home Assistant OS hosts unreachable.
body: Home Assistant corrects a network setting that could make affected Home Assistant OS installations unreachable when using a virtual network, or VLAN, created by Supervisor. The problem involves the Realtek r8169 network driver and the kernel included in Home Assistant OS 18.3.

Samant Maharaj makes Supervisor explicitly apply the usual VLAN header setting. Existing connections receive the correction when Supervisor next starts. This is his first contribution to Supervisor, reviewed by Stefan Agner.

pullRequests.title: Fix missing VLAN reorder headers flag

articles.title: ESPHome keeps solar export from corrupting emonTx energy totals
articles.dek: Reverse power flow stops being mistaken for a meter reset in Home Assistant’s statistics.
body: ESPHome corrects how emonTx and emon32 meters feed Home Assistant’s long-term energy statistics. Their net total can decrease during solar export, but ESPHome had labelled it as a counter that only increases, causing those decreases to be treated as meter resets.

Frédéric Metrich changes the default to allow energy to flow in both directions. Pulse counters retain their increasing-only behavior, and explicitly configured overrides stay in place. J. Nick Koston reviewed the implementation.

[emontx] Energy sensors use the total state class

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps unrelated CD tracks separate
articles.dek: Dummy recording identifiers in older CD-ripping files no longer make different songs look identical.
body: Music Assistant stops treating a placeholder recording identifier as proof that unrelated songs are the same recording. Some files describing CD rips from older Exact Audio Copy versions carry an all-zero identifier, which could cause tracks from different albums to collapse into one library entry.

OzGav makes matching ignore invalid identifiers already stored, preventing further false matches without a rescan. Newly read local files also discard bad identifiers and log which file needs attention. Previously combined entries are not rebuilt by this change. Marvin Schenkel reviewed the correction.

pullRequests.title: Stop placeholder ISRCs from merging unrelated tracks

articles.title: Assist honours Gemma’s faster response setting
articles.dek: The minimal-thinking option stops being ignored for Gemma 4 models on Google’s API.
body: Home Assistant sends the selected thinking level to Gemma 4 models used through Google’s Generative AI connection. The setting had been ignored for these models, leaving Assist waiting while the model performed its default reasoning.

Contributor tronikos tested the change against Google’s live API. With minimal thinking, the gemma-4-26b-a4b-it model responded in about one second rather than roughly five to fourteen seconds. Only minimal and high are sent for Gemma 4; unsupported levels retain the API’s default behaviour.

pullRequests.title: Send thinking level for Gemma 4 models in Google Generative AI

articles.title: Home Assistant stops one SolarEdge inverter delaying another
articles.dek: Repeated checks for unsupported controls could make a working inverter appear unavailable.
body: Home Assistant stops repeatedly waiting for unsupported controls on SolarEdge inverters sharing a connection. One inverter could leave the other waiting behind unanswered requests every fifteen minutes, making a working device appear unavailable.

Franck Nijhof stops rechecking control groups that remain silent after setup and its first follow-up check. In the reported configuration, the expected wait drops from fifty seconds to ten. Checks for attached batteries and meters continue; a control that starts responding much later needs an integration reload.

pullRequests.title: Stop asking a SolarEdge inverter about blocks it never answers

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps saved music visible in filtered searches
articles.dek: Searching a single service stops hiding library items, while global results avoid showing them twice.
body: Music Assistant keeps music from the library in search results when the listener searches only one connected service, such as Tidal. Previously, it removed items as duplicates of the library while leaving the library’s own results out, making saved music disappear entirely.
Marcel van der Veldt coordinates the server and interface corrections so a search across the library and services still lists each linked item only once. The filtering also covers radio stations.
